title: Forbidden Keyword Content Filter
real_world_story: Community moderation is critical for maintaining a safe environment in real-time chat platforms. To automatically flag toxic content, the system employs a high-performance string-matching engine that scans incoming messages for forbidden keywords. To avoid the quadratic complexity of naive searching, the platform implements the Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) algorithm, which uses a precomputed failure function to skip unnecessary comparisons and ensure linear-time scanning.
problem_statement: Given a chat message and a forbidden keyword, find all occurrences of the keyword within the message. Your implementation must use the KMP algorithm to ensure optimal time complexity.
task: Find and return all starting indices (0-indexed) where the forbidden keyword appears in the chat message. Return the indices in ascending order, or -1 if the keyword is not found.
input_format: The first line contains the chat message string. The second line contains the forbidden keyword string.
output_format: A space-separated list of starting indices in ascending order, or -1.

examples.input: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog\nthe
examples.explanation: The keyword 'the' appears at index 0 and index 31.

real_world_takeaway: The KMP algorithm is a cornerstone of efficient text processing, allowing systems to search for patterns in massive streams of data without redundant backtracking, making it ideal for real-time content moderation.
